definitions.explanation: Lines or surfaces that maintain equal distance and never intersect.
Doing multiple things at the same time.

examples.japanese: この{二|ふた}つの{線|せん}は{平行|へいこう}だ。
{線路|せんろ}は{平行|へいこう}に{走|はし}っている。
examples.english: The railroad tracks run parallel to each other.

examples.japanese: {平行|へいこう}な{二|ふた}つの{線|せん}はどこまで{伸|の}ばしても{交|まじ}わらない。
examples.english: Two parallel lines never intersect no matter how far they are extended.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}と{勉強|べんきょう}を{平行|へいこう}して{進|すす}める。
examples.english: To pursue work and studies simultaneously.

examples.japanese: {二|ふた}つのプロジェクトを{平行|へいこう}して{進|すす}めている。
examples.english: We are working on two projects simultaneously.

examples.japanese: {話|はな}し{合|あ}いは{平行線|へいこうせん}のままで、なかなか{結論|けつろん}が{出|で}なかった。
examples.english: The discussion remained at a stalemate, and no conclusion was reached.
examples.notes: {平行線|へいこうせん} (parallel lines) is used figuratively to mean that two sides cannot reach agreement.

notes:
{平行|へいこう} has both geometric and figurative meanings.

GEOMETRIC SENSE:
- Lines that never meet regardless of how far they extend
- {平行線|へいこうせん}: parallel lines

FIGURATIVE SENSE:
- Doing things at the same time
- {平行|へいこう}して: simultaneously

RELATED TERMS:
- {垂直|すいちょく}: perpendicular, vertical
- {平行四辺形|へいこうしへんけい}: parallelogram
